scope: Adds three direct cross-paradigm multi-hop evidence-compression sources to the eight v2 architecture/KV sources. Complete code, backward/forward citations, proceedings, patents, deployed systems, non-English literature, and independent expert review remain mandatory.

additional_sources.title: BRIEF: Bridging Retrieval and Inference for Multi-hop Reasoning via Compression
additional_sources.relevant_claim: decompose multi-hop questions, require a helpful proposition for every hop from distinct documents, and concatenate all propositions as a compression target

additional_sources.title: BRIEF-Pro: Universal Context Compression with Short-to-Long Synthesis for Fast and Accurate Multi-Hop Reasoning
additional_sources.relevant_claim: long oracle-plus-distractor compression, per-sentence helpfulness, controllable budgets, whole-pipeline cost, and one-missing-hop error analysis

additional_sources.title: IterCOMP: Reasoning-aware Adaptive Prompt Compression for Multi-hop Question Answering
additional_sources.relevant_claim: Full versus Partial all-hop evidence, answerability judgment, missing-information identification, targeted follow-up, and iterative evidence accumulation

new_overlap_decisions.reason: BRIEF rejects synthetic examples missing a helpful proposition for any decomposed hop, requires distinct source documents, and concatenates every hop proposition
IterCOMP explicitly defines Full as all required hop sub-answers and Partial as a missing suffix, evaluates answerability, and models premature stopping
IterCOMP identifies the next missing subquestion and iteratively accumulates targeted evidence until judged sufficient
BRIEF-Pro trains on 6K-word oracle-plus-distractor contexts, preserves compacted oracle documents, exposes requested/automatic summary budgets, and reports missing-one-hop failures
BRIEF scores proposition inclusion and BRIEF-Pro scores sentence removal using target-answer likelihood

surviving_hypotheses.statement: A preregistered small set of causal information-flow quantities predicts unseen from-scratch recurrent/global placements at fixed state and compute better than search, sensitivity, role, and random-placement baselines.

A cheap pre-output statistic computed from internal compressed or sparse model state predicts held-out multi-hop failure beyond external evidence coverage and LLM sufficiency judgments, answer-span importance, GER/reachability/consensus, attention mass, and output reconstruction error, with equal-physical-budget interventions moving statistic and outcome together.
concessions: the conjunction over all hop-specific sources is prior art
complete-versus-partial sufficiency testing is prior art
identifying and retrieving missing evidence is prior art
query-aware source-complete multi-hop compression is prior art
routing, reachability, global answer erasure, and survive-but-not-used framing are prior art
required_baselines: BRIEF per-hop proposition coverage and target-answer helpfulness
BRIEF-Pro oracle-document coverage, leave-one-sentence-out helpfulness, and requested budgets
IterCOMP Full/Partial answerability score and missing-information judgment
GER, compressed token-graph reachability, and head consensus
Ada-KV retained mass and output-error bound
single-source, top-k, random, recency, distance, load, and answer-length controls
held_out: unseen graphs, hop counts, and necessary-source counts
unseen compression rates and state budgets
a different KV compression or native sparse-attention family
surviving_hypotheses.success: a predictor frozen before held-out outputs materially improves calibration/discrimination beyond every baseline and predicts equal-physical-budget single-source removal/restoration effects across real documents, scales, and a held-out mechanism
falsifiers: external source coverage or an LLM sufficiency judge predicts equally well
GER/reachability/consensus, mass, or reconstruction error predicts equally well
source labels or predictor form change after held-out outputs
equal-budget removal/restoration does not move outcomes as predicted
effect disappears after base difficulty, distance, load, answer length, and source-count controls
relationship fails on real documents, another scale, or another mechanism

rejected_hypotheses.reason: BRIEF and IterCOMP explicitly operationalize complete per-hop evidence and missing-source recovery, while BRIEF-Pro scales source-aware compression and audits one-hop omission
the conjunction remains useful as a measured feature but cannot itself be claimed as a new composition principle

code_followup.brief_and_brief_pro: one evolving combined repository is declared and currently includes training/evaluation/model/data links, but its immutable tree, root rights, dataset/model revisions, and historical BRIEF-v2 correspondence are unaudited
code_followup.itercomp: no dedicated code artifact is declared on the arXiv record

full_landscape_before_claim: audit immutable BRIEF/BRIEF-Pro repository, model, dataset, environment, and license identities
audit STEC and other July-August 2026 evidence-compression work before treating this search as current
follow backward and forward citations for N1 and the residual N2 empirical-law question
search proceedings, patents, deployed systems, technical reports, and non-English literature with dated queries
build a claim-granular closest-overlap table and obtain independent expert review
evidence_before_claim: freeze source labels, predictor, models, mechanisms, splits, and analysis before held-out outputs
compare all mandatory internal and external baselines
use at least three scales and a held-out mechanism with paired uncertainty
hold out document/domain, graph/hop, rate/budget, and architecture cells
perform equal-physical-budget removal and restoration interventions
claim_gate.decision: No N2 concept may be claimed novel. Only a prospectively demonstrated incremental internal-state law could reopen novelty review; otherwise N2 is an evaluation framework contribution or is removed.

decision.next_action: audit STEC and the BRIEF repository/model/data boundary, then complete citation review before deciding whether the residual N2 empirical-law protocol is worth freezing
